findings.title: Off-by-one error in section size check
findings.description: The ELF parser incorrectly rejects valid ELF sections that end exactly at the end of the file due to an off-by-one error in bounds checking. The root cause is the use of `>=` instead of `>` when comparing the section range end against the ELF file size. This leads to a false OutOfBounds error being triggered for legitimate sections. An attacker could craft an ELF file with a section ending precisely at the file boundary, causing the Solana runtime to reject a valid program. The impact is denial of service for valid programs, degrading usability and potentially breaking backward compatibility.

findings.title: Read-only region can overlap stack
findings.description: The read-only memory region in the BPF virtual machine can overlap with the stack region due to incorrect bounds checks during ELF loading. The vulnerability arises because the validation logic only checks if the virtual address (vaddr) exceeds the stack start, rather than checking if the combined vaddr and section size exceeds it. This allows a maliciously crafted ELF to define a read-only section that starts before but extends into the stack region. As a result, parts of the read-only data become unaddressable or shadowed by the stack, leading to incorrect program behavior when accessing such data. The impact is potential misbehavior of BPF programs, which could result in denial of service or logic errors in program execution.
